releases.notes:
# GUI Shop 2.1.0

This is the first release to support multiple Minecraft versions from a single build. Supports
Minecraft 1.21.x, 26.1, 26.2, and 26.3.

## Shop data migration

Shop configs now live in per-shop `.snbt` files under `config/gui-shop/shops/`, tagged with the
game's data version. Existing shops migrate automatically on first load, no manual steps needed.
Once the migration is confirmed successful, the old `guishop.json`/`guishopeconomy.json` files are
renamed to `.pre-migration-backup`. These aren't cleaned up automatically, feel free to delete
them once you've confirmed everything migrated correctly.

## New features

- Balance limit raised from 2^31 to 2^63
- Shop items now upgrade through Minecraft's own item data fixer, same as vanilla inventory items.
- Selling an item now pays out less if it's damaged, has a higher repair cost, or has a different
  custom name compared to the listed item. A player can no longer sell a worn, repaired, or
  renamed item for full price.
- Shop menu got a back button, returning the player to the shop list at the page you came from.
  (requested by @ZerasT, #3)
- Balance command now shows the currency's display name instead of its internal ID.
- Added back support for all Minecraft 1.21 versions. (requested by @neondungeon, #7)

## Bug fixes

- Fixed pagination not showing when browsing shops. (reported by @rickiewars, #3)
- Fixed `/guishop removeitem` leaking shop names via tab-complete to players without the remove
  permission.
- Fixed a crash on first startup of a new world, where the shop database was created before the
  world directory existed.
- Fixed enchanted items failing to save to a shop. (reported by @ZerasT, #4)
- Fixed a crash when an economy account referenced a currency that didn't exist, such accounts
  are now skipped with a warning instead. (reported by @rickiewars, #2)

## Stability

I've significantly grown the mod's automated test coverage, including the code that talks
directly to Minecraft. The goal is to catch bugs on every supported Minecraft version before a
release ships, not after you're already running it.

Shop items now upgrade through Minecraft's own item data fixer instead of custom logic, the same
mechanism vanilla uses on your inventory. This should prevent enchantments or other item data from
getting lost or corrupted across Minecraft version updates.

---

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/rickiewars/gui-shop/compare/2.0.0+1.21.11...2.1.0

releases.notes:
# GUIShop V2.0

Version 2.0 focuses on long-term stability, maintainability, and extensibility.

From this release onward, new features are developed with automated tests in place. Most core logic is now covered by tests (current code coverage: 41%), and care is taken to avoid breaking existing installations. Where changes are required, migrations are provided to ensure smooth upgrades.

## New features

- Shop selection menu: a new menu allows players to select which shop to open.
- New command aliases: /shop, /buy, and /trade now open the shop selection menu. These aliases are registered only if they are not already used by another mod, preventing conflicts.
- Multiple currencies per shop: shops can now use multiple currencies, and the balance of all currencies is shown when hovering over the currency slot.

This release is considered stable and suitable for production use. Future development may introduce new features. Support will be limited to major issues.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/rickiewars/gui-shop/compare/1.4.10+1.21.5...2.0.0+1.21.5
